rejectedAlternative.description: Original HB-02 bytes before the Sep-12 tightjeans refit
rejectedAlternative.whatItWouldFailToCatch: Keeping the HB-02 pin would make the falsifier track a lineage that no longer ships. The promoted row in the report tracks the tightjeans lineage (69067 tris), which is the actual shipped body. A broken station on the tightjeans lineage would go undetected because the falsifier would still compare against the HB-02 baseline (68214 tris). The test would pass even if the tightjeans decimation produced wrong results.

rationale: The falsifier must track the lineage that actually ships to learners. The promoted row in the evidence report (humanoid-postopt-ladder-face-preserving-2026-09-11.json) tracks the tightjeans lineage (69067 tris, rederivedFrom 57e27730). The test now re-runs the recorded fp-r0.4 rung on the committed tightjeans pre-image (57e27730) and asserts equality against both the fp-r0.4-jeans-lineage sweep entry AND the promoted row. Both assertions now pass because they describe the same lineage.
whatTheRetargetedClauseStillFalsifies: A broken face-preserving station on the tightjeans lineage: if iterate-optimize.ts --face-preserving --face-preserving-ratio 0.4 on the 57e27730 pre-image produces a triangle count != 69067 or face count != 52778, the test fails
A regression in the rung technique (selective weld+simplifyPrimitive at ratio 0.4, error 0.01 on non-face meshes) that alters face triangle count or total triangle count on the tightjeans input
A silent change to the tightjeans pre-image that would cause the recorded rung to produce different output
The promoted row drifting from what the recorded station actually produces on the committed pre-image
